questions.question_text:
The five-number summary of a town's daily temperatures ($^{\circ}\text{C}$) is $\text{Min} = 10^{\circ}\text{C}$, $Q_1 = 17^{\circ}\text{C}$, $Q_2 = 25^{\circ}\text{C}$, $Q_3 = 38^{\circ}\text{C}$, $\text{Max} = 45^{\circ}\text{C}$.
Find the interquartile range.

options.why: Computed the range (Max minus Min) instead of the interquartile range.
Added $Q_1$ and $Q_3$ instead of subtracting.
Used the median and lower quartile instead of the upper and lower quartiles.

questions.question_text:
The daily temperatures ($^{\circ}\text{C}$) for $8$ days, listed in ascending order, are:
$6, 8, 10, 12, 12, 13, 15, 17$
A $9$th day, an unseasonal heatwave of $35^{\circ}\text{C}$, is added to the dataset.
Find the new interquartile range.

options.why: Assumed the IQR stays exactly the same as before, without recomputing $Q_1$ and $Q_3$ for the new dataset.
Computed the new range instead of the new interquartile range.
Treated the new outlier value itself as $Q_3$ instead of recomputing the upper quartile properly.

questions.question_text: Calculate the interquartile range of the data list $2,5,6,9,12,16,22,25,31,35,42,45$.

options.why: Uses the upper end of the data rather than subtracting the lower quartile from the upper quartile.
Does not use the half-way averages for the quartiles in this 12-value list.
Rounds or calculates the quartiles incorrectly.

questions.solution_text: The lower-half median is $Q_1=(6+9)/2=7.5$. The upper-half median is $Q_3=(31+35)/2=33$. Thus IQR $=33-7.5=25.5$.

questions.question_text:
Why is the range a problematic measure of spread for this set of data?
$-3,-1,2,3,3,5,6,7,7,7,8,9,10,11,12,46$.

options.why: Negative values do not prevent the range from being calculated or interpreted.

options.text: Because some of the numbers are repeated
options.why: Repeated values do not make the range an unreliable measure of spread.

options.text: Because there is an even number of pieces of data
options.why: The number of data values does not affect the calculation of the range.

questions.solution_text: The range is maximum minus minimum, so it is dominated by the unusually large value 46. That outlier makes the range much larger than the spread of most of the data.
